description: Aura Phase-D = masterplan Phase 1C (Question Gate). Closes Phase 1. Design v2 (nanobot-aligned, see docs/phase-01c-question-gate-scope.md): ask_user is a regular tool with exclusive semantics. Model decides when to use it (system prompt teaches cardinal cases). Pause = run.Status='waiting_for_user' (column exists since Phase 1A). Resume = standard tool_result message from next inbound. NO new chat_questions table, NO new event types, NO custom action grammar. Simpler than the v1 design, aligned with nanobot/LangGraph/Codex industry patterns. Telegram renders numbered-text options (NOT inline keyboard — required for cmd/probe_chat E2E automation). Each story = ONE atomic commit on master.

userStories.title: ask_user tool + agent loop pause via sentinel error + pending-call detection helper
userStories.description: Adopt the nanobot pattern as a regular tool in Aura's registry. (a) internal/agent/tools/registry/ask_user.go (new) implements the Tool interface: Name='ask_user'; Description spells out PRD §5.2.5 cardinal cases (when to use, when NOT); Parameters JSONSchema = {question string required, options []string optional 2-4, kind string optional enum clarification|approval default clarification}; Execute returns a typed sentinel error tools.ErrAwaitingUserInput wrapping the question/options/kind. (b) internal/agent/loop.go: detect the sentinel error from executor return; when present, set run.Status='waiting_for_user' (column already in storage/runs from Phase 1A), set Stats.StopReason='waiting_for_user', return from runLoop without dispatching further tool calls or LLM rounds. The original tool_call entry stays in run_events as the pending marker. (c) New helper agent.PendingAskUserCall(events []runs.Event) (toolCallID string, options []string, kind string, ok bool) — walks the event log backward, finds the most recent tool_call for ask_user that has no matching tool_result. Mirrors nanobot's pending_ask_user_id. (d) The tool is exclusive in spirit: if the LLM batches ask_user with other tool calls in one turn, the loop processes ask_user FIRST (which pauses) and discards the rest of the batch (they'll re-emit on resume). (e) Tests: tool definition shape, Execute returns sentinel, loop pauses on sentinel, PendingAskUserCall finds pending, returns nothing on resolved (matching tool_result exists), returns nothing when ask_user absent.

userStories.title: System-prompt teaches when to use ask_user + eval fixture
userStories.description: Aura's canonical system prompt gains a 'Clarification and Approval Protocol' section so the LLM knows when to use ask_user. Per the design pivot, code-side has NO hardcoded risk list — the prompt is the policy. (a) Locate the system-prompt assembly point (likely internal/agent/promptplan.go or internal/conversation/system_prompt.go). (b) Add a section with: (i) cardinal cases that DO justify ask_user (PRD §5.2.5 verbatim: missing required slot; ambiguous viable interpretations; irreversible destructive action; permission escalation; durable user-memory write without explicit intent; 3+ recoverable tool failures); (ii) cardinal non-cases (clear instruction; low-risk reversible default; resolvable by reading wiki/context; resolvable by a search tool); (iii) the two kinds explained — clarification (2-4 generated options + free-text allowed) vs approval (canonical options approve_once|approve_session|approve_persist|deny|cancel); (iv) at least 1 clarification example + 1 approval example as concrete tool_call illustrations; (v) 2 counter-examples (when NOT to ask). (c) Eval fixture at internal/agent/ask_user_promptfx_test.go: a Go test with a table of (description, user_input, expected_emit bool, rationale) — documents the contract. Does NOT run an actual LLM. Acts as the agreed contract for future eval slices.
